record.original_question: Classify low-dimensional varieties whose second and/or third secant variety has minimal degree; more generally, for a fixed r, construct varieties X such that σ_r(X) is a hypersurface of the smallest possible degree.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Classify varieties of small dimension having second and (or) third secant variety of minimal degree. More generally, given r, produce a variety X such that σr (X) is a hypersurface of the smallest possible degree.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Work over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. For a non-degenerate irreducible projective variety X ⊂ P^N, the r-th secant variety σ_r(X) is the Zariski closure of the union of linear spans of r-tuples of points of X:
   σ_r(X) = closure of ⋃ ⟨x_1,...,x_r⟩, where x_1,...,x_r ∈ X.
When σ_r(X) is a hypersurface in P^N (i.e. has codimension one), one says it is of minimal degree if its degree attains the smallest value possible given the dimension and embedding data. (A variety Y ⊂ P^N of codimension c has minimal degree if deg(Y) = c + 1; this is the lower bound for non-degenerate varieties.)

Problem.
(a) Classify all non-degenerate irreducible projective varieties X of small dimension whose second secant variety σ_2(X) is a hypersurface of minimal degree, and analogously for the third secant variety σ_3(X).
(b) More generally, given an integer r ≥ 2, construct non-degenerate irreducible projective varieties X ⊂ P^N such that σ_r(X) is a hypersurface of the smallest possible degree.
artifact.status_search_result: A general classification of varieties whose higher secant variety is a hypersurface of minimal degree does not appear in the literature. Partial results exist: del Pezzo–Bertini classifies varieties of minimal degree; recent work (e.g. determinantal characterizations of higher secant varieties of minimal degree, and characterizations of secant varieties of Severi varieties among cubic hypersurfaces) gives structural results in special cases, but a full low-dimensional classification and a general construction for arbitrary r are not established.

status_evidence.title: Determinantal characterization of higher secant varieties of minimal degree
status_evidence.snippet: Higher secant varieties of minimal degree have determinantal presentations of two types (scroll type and Veronese type), generalizing del Pezzo–Bertini.
status_evidence.claim: Partial structural results exist for higher secant varieties of minimal degree, but a complete classification is not given.

status_evidence.title: Characterization of Secant Varieties of Severi Varieties Among Cubic Hypersurfaces
status_evidence.snippet: An irreducible cubic hypersurface ... is the secant variety of a Severi variety iff its Lie algebra of infinitesimal linear automorphisms admits a nonzero prolongation.
status_evidence.claim: Special-case characterizations exist (e.g. Severi varieties giving cubic secant hypersurfaces), supporting that the general problem is still under investigation.
